chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ibrahim ibn Is'haq, from Muhammad ibn Suleyman al-Daylami, from Abu Hajar al-Aslami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who comes to Makkah as a pilgrim and does not visit me in Al-Medina, I shall turn away from him on the Day of Judgement; and the one who comes to me as a visitor, my intercession is obligated for him; and the one for whom my intercession is obligated, Paradise is obligated for him.'

And the one who dies in one of the two Sanctuaries, Makkah and Al-Medina, will not be exposed (to scrutiny) and will not be reckoned with; and the one who dies as an emigrant to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will be resurrected on the Day of Judgement along with the companions of Badr.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the Prophet in Medina during Hajj?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this hadith from al-Kafi underscores the spiritual necessity of combining Hajj with Ziyarat al-Nabi, linking the Prophet’s personal intercession (Shafa'ah) directly to entry into Paradise. It further elevates the status of those who die in the two holy sanctuaries (Makkah and Madinah) or as Muhajirun, associating them with the elite companions of Badr, a connection often interpreted through the lens of divine favor and exemption from rigorous accountability.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar, from Ibrahim Bin Is’haq, from Muhammad Bin Suleyman Al Dalaymi, from Abu Hajar Al Aslamy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘The one who comes to Makkah as a pilgrim and does not perform mysaww Ziyarah in Al-Medina, Isaww shall turn away from him on the Day of Judgement; and the one who comes to mesaww as a visitor, mysaww intercession would be Obligated upon him; and the one for whom mysaww intercession is Obligated, the Paradise would be Obligated for him.

And the one who dies in one of the two Harrams, Makkah and Al-Medina, would not be exposed (on the Day of Judgement), and would not be Reckoned with; and the one who dies as an emigrant to Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic, would be Resurrected on the Day of Judgement along with the companions of (the battle of) Badr’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bandar has narrated from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq from Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Daylamiy from abu Hajar al- Aslamiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,

has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘Whoever comes to Makkah for al-Hajj but does not visit me, on the Day of Judgment I will turn away from him. Whoever comes to visit me, my intercession on his behalf becomes necessary. One on whose behalf my intercession becomes necessary, for him paradise becomes necessary.

Whoever dies in one of the two Sacred areas, Makkah or al-Madinah, will not be exposed or brought in, to present an account of his deeds. Whoever dies during his migration to Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, on the Day of Judgment will be raised with the people of Badr.’”
